verdict.rationale: Lithic documents the core building blocks for issuing agent-scoped cards — virtual card creation, merchant-category/velocity/amount authorization rules at the card level, spend limits, and an explicit blog post walking through creating a test card, configuring authorization rules, and running transactions against them for agentic use cases (lithic-docs-9, lithic-docs-3, lithic-docs-13, lithic-docs-11/21). It also explicitly markets 'secure and autonomous issuing... for AI-powered workflows' (lithic-docs-12) and an MCP server letting agents act on card program policies (lithic-docs-22). However, there is no single named product/feature called out as 'AI agent card' with built-in expiry-for-agent or agent-specific scoping in one bundled offering — it requires composing card creation + rules + spend limits + expiry manually rather than a documented one-step 'agent card' primitive. missing for 10: a first-party named 'agent card' or 'AI agent issuing' product feature bundling merchant lock+cap+expiry in one call, and independent/hands-on confirmation of an agent actually using such a card end-to-end.
